artists.biography: Gene were an English alternative rock quartet that rose to prominence in the mid-1990s. Formed in 1993, they were popularly labelled as a Britpop band and often drew comparisons to The Smiths because of their Morrissey-esque lead singer, Martin Rossiter. Gene's music was influenced by The Jam, The Small Faces, The Style Council and The Clash.

The Albums" by Gene is an expansive box set released in 2020 by Demon Records, compiling the British rock band’s complete studio discography. The collection features all four of Gene’s original studio albums—Olympian (1995), Drawn to the Deep End (1997), Revelations (1999), and Libertine (2001)—alongside additional material such as B-sides and demos. Musically, Gene’s work is rooted in Britpop and alternative rock, drawing clear inspiration from bands like The Smiths, The Jam, and The Faces. Their sound is characterized by Martin Rossiter’s literate, emotive vocals, Steve Mason’s melodic guitar lines, and a tight rhythm section, blending introspective lyrics with anthemic melodies.

Within Gene’s discography, "The Albums" serves as a comprehensive retrospective, capturing the band’s evolution from their early indie success to their later, more experimental work. The box set highlights Gene’s consistent songwriting and their ability to balance pop sensibilities with deeper emotional resonance. While each individual album received positive critical attention upon its original release—particularly Olympian and Drawn to the Deep End, which both reached No. 8 on the UK Albums Chart—the 2020 box set was praised for its thorough presentation and high-quality vinyl pressings, reaffirming Gene’s legacy as one of the most respected acts of the Britpop era.
